title: The Poisson-Dirichlet law for prime predecessors
main_claim: Take a uniformly random prime p ≤ x. The normalized log-sizes log q_j / log(p-1) of the prime factors of p-1, ranked in decreasing order, converge in all finite joint distributions to Poisson-Dirichlet(1). This resolves the Ford-Konyagin-Luca conjecture, and it also gives the shifted-prime Dickman asymptotic #{p≤x : P+(p-1) ≤ x^{1/u}} ~ π(x)ρ(u) for each fixed u.

issues.description: The two-sided correlation theorem rests on operator results imported from the companion paper S (Theorem 3.5, Corollary 3.11, Lemma 3.4, Theorem 4.1, Lemma 4.3). I checked that the hypotheses as stated in S match how they are used here. S Definition 2.1: T = log L, group ranges a<b<c<d<0.47, a first endpoint independent of the marks with sup ≤ exp(O(√L)), fixed J, and the ban on free labels. I did not re-audit the proofs in S. The correctness of the main theorem therefore depends on S. This is not a circular dependence, because S does not use this paper.
issues.evidence: "This is the combination of the local transference theorem, endpoint pairing corollary, and physical Schur bound of S [Theorem 3.5, Corollary 3.11, and Lemma 3.4]"; "This is S [Theorem 4.1 and Lemma 4.3]."

issues.description: The paper proves its own Vinogradov-Korobov-type bound for prime polynomials up to height x^2 by re-deriving the mean-value method. I checked that the claimed strength is consistent with known zero-free regions: the saving exp(-c L^{1/3-o(1)}) comfortably exceeds L^{-A}. I did not verify every step of the degree-uniform mean-value iteration.
issues.evidence: Lemma lp:prime-polynomial: |Σ_{p∈I} χ(p) p^{-1+it}| ≪ L^{-A} for L^{B0} ≤ |t| ≤ x^2, x^τ/2 ≤ N ≤ x^η, q ≤ L^C
